title: A COVENANT FOR GENERATIONS TO COME

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "I am making this covenant, with its oath, not only with you who are standing here with us today in the presence of the Lord our God but also with those who are not here today." — Deut 29:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a striking thought: God was making this covenant not only with those physically standing there that day, but also "with those who are not here today." The covenant reached beyond that generation to embrace their children and descendants yet unborn. God's purposes were never limited to one moment; they stretched forward into the future.

There is great encouragement in this for us. The God who thinks in generations is at work in ways far larger than our single lifetime. When we walk faithfully with God, we are part of something that extends beyond us — a legacy of faith passed down, a covenant reaching to those "not here yet."

This should shape how we live and pray. We labour, teach, and pray not only for ourselves but for those who will come after us — our children, grandchildren, and spiritual descendants we may never meet. The faithfulness we sow today can bear fruit in lives we will never see on this side of eternity.

And in a real sense, we ourselves are among "those not here today." On that day in Moab, God had His eye on future generations who would come to trust Him — including all who would one day be gathered into His people through Christ. The gospel invitation reaches across time to "all whom the Lord our God will call" (Acts 2:39). You were on God's heart long before you were born. His covenant love is that vast.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I living and praying with future generations in mind?
2. How does it move me that God's covenant reached ahead to include me?
3. What legacy of faith can I begin sowing today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that Your covenant love reaches across generations, even to me. Help me live faithfully for those who come after me, sowing a legacy of faith. Amen.
